identity.title: Dynamical Equilibrium in the Molecular ISM in 28 Nearby Star-forming Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: we combine arcsecond resolution CO data from PHANGS-ALMA with multi-wavelength data that traces the atomic gas, stellar structure, and star formation rate (SFR) for 28 nearby star-forming galaxies.

targets.name: 28 PHANGS-ALMA nearby star-forming galaxies (e.g. NGC 628, NGC 3627, NGC 4321)

evidence.quote: (2) Distance (from the Extragalactic Distance Database; (cite: Tully_etal_2009)); (3) inclination angle (cite: Lang_etal_2019)
(2) Distance (from the Extragalactic Distance Database; (cite: Tully_etal_2009)); (3) inclination angle (cite: Lang_etal_2019)

question.value: Does the observed turbulent pressure in molecular gas match the dynamical equilibrium pressure required to support the ISM in the galactic gravitational potential, on kpc and cloud scales?

evidence.quote: We compare the observed turbulent pressure in molecular gas, $P_\mathrm{turb}$, to the required pressure for the interstellar gas to stay in equilibrium in the gravitational potential of a galaxy, $P_\mathrm{DE}$.
We use PHANGS-ALMA $\mathrm{CO}\,(2\text{--}1)$ data (internal release version 3.4)

They include data from both the 12-m array and the Morita Atacama Compact Array (ACA; consisting of the 7-m array and four 12-m total power antennas), and therefore should recover emission on all spatial scales.
The angular resolution (i.e., beam FWHM) ranges between $1.0\ensuremath{''}$–$1.8\ensuremath{''}$, corresponding to 25–120 pc linear resolution at the targets’ distances.
The 1$\sigma$ noise level in the data is $0.2\text{--}0.3$ K in a $2.5\,\mbox{$\rm km\,s^{-1}$}$ channel.

provided.value: HI 21 cm maps for atomic gas

evidence.quote: We include new VLA data from the PHANGS-VLA project (covering 11 targets in our sample; PI: D. Utomo)
We use *Spitzer* IRAC 3.6 $\mu$m data to trace the stellar mass distribution.

evidence.quote: We combine GALEX near-UV (NUV) data and WISE mid-IR (MIR) data to derive kpc-scale star formation rate (SFR) estimates.

method.value: Convolve CO cubes to 60/120 pc and 1 kpc, build moment maps, tile footprint in 1 kpc hexagonal apertures

evidence.quote: we quantify a CO flux recovery fraction, $f_\mathrm{CO,\,\theta pc}$, within each 1 kpc aperture.

method.value: Sigma_mol = alpha_CO/R21 I_CO; metallicity-dependent alpha_CO; HI, 3.6um, NUV+12um conversions

evidence.quote: $R_{21} = 0.7$ is the adopted $\mathrm{CO}\,(2\text{--}1)$ to $\mathrm{CO}\,(1\text{--}0)$ line ratio
This conversion assumes a 3.6 $\mu$m mass-to-light ratio of $Y_{3.6} = 0.47\,M_\odot/L_\odot$ (cite: McGaugh_Schombert_2014).
we re-derive our key measurements using three alternative $\alpha_\mathrm{CO}$ prescriptions, and compare them with our fiducial prescription.

method.value: P_turb = 3 Sigma sigma^2/(2D) with D = beam FWHM; P_DE at kpc scale and cloud scale (weight of clouds + atomic layer); CO-intensity weighted averages

evidence.quote: we assume a constant density spherical cloud filling each beam, with the cloud diameter $D_\mathrm{cloud}$ equal to the beam FWHM
We adopt a fixed atomic gas velocity dispersion $\sigma_\mathrm{atom}=10\;\mbox{$\rm km\,s^{-1}$}$

assumptions.value: Turbulence dominates internal pressure; dark matter neglected

evidence.quote: we assume in this work that turbulent motion represents the primary source of internal pressure in molecular gas, and treat all other contributions as sub-dominant.

findings_qualitative.value: Cloud-scale dynamical equilibrium holds in disk regions; bulge/bar regions show higher P_turb

evidence.quote: many measurements in bulge or bar regions show systematically higher $\left<P_\mathrm{turb,\,\theta pc}\right>$.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas pressure equals smooth-disk kpc-scale P_DE
claims.experiment: Compare P_turb to P_DE,1kpc in 1762 apertures
claims.result: P_turb exceeds P_DE,1kpc, median factor 2.8 at 120 pc
claims.finding: Molecular gas is over-pressurized relative to the smooth-disk estimate

evidence.quote: We find that $P_\mathrm{turb}$ correlates with, but almost always exceeds the estimated $P_\mathrm{DE}$ on kiloparsec scales.

claims.experiment: Cloud-scale P_DE including self-gravity, external gravity and ambient pressure
claims.finding: Dynamical equilibrium holds on cloud scales

evidence.quote: a revised estimate of $P_\mathrm{DE}$ on cloud scales, which accounts for molecular gas self-gravity, external gravity, and ambient pressure, agrees well with the observed $P_\mathrm{turb}$ in galaxy disks.

claims.experiment: Compare Sigma_SFR with P_turb and P_DE
claims.finding: Consistent with feedback-driven momentum injection, if SF clumping is considered

evidence.quote: The correlation between $\Sigma_\mathrm{SFR}$ and kpc-scale $P_\mathrm{DE}$ in galaxy disks is consistent with the expectation from self-regulated star formation models.

why_this_method.value: Top-down aperture approach avoids cloud identification and handles marginally resolved data

evidence.quote: it is designed to robustly treat data with a wide range of physical resolutions, even when individual gas structures are not fully resolved or cleanly separated from one another.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CPROPS cloud segmentation with spherical geometry gives P_turb below P_DE by ~0.66 dex; fixed 120 pc depth restores agreement

evidence.quote: On average, this offset is about 0.66 dex.

limitations_admitted.value: Sensitivity censoring biases slope shallower; systematics dominate fit errors

evidence.loc: Predicting Turbulent Pressure from Kpc-scale Equilibrium Pressure
evidence.quote: This means that our cloud-scale measurements cannot probe as low molecular gas surface density as our kpc-scale measurements do, and our pressure estimates suffer from a similar censoring effect.

referee_caveats_inferred: Uniform-sphere with D = beam FWHM sets P_turb scale and resolution dependence
P_turb and P_DE both scale with alpha_CO so their agreement is partly built in
Metallicity predicted from a global relation, not measured
The 1 kpc scale and stellar scale heights are assumed
